patterns.title: Assistant-style preface
patterns.rationale: The sentence describes the assistant's action instead of belonging to the document.
patterns.action: Delete the preface and begin with the deliverable.

patterns.title: Process narration
patterns.rationale: The prose narrates editing rather than communicating the subject.
patterns.action: Remove the process claim or replace it with the concrete content.

patterns.title: Assistant closing offer
patterns.pattern: (?im)^(?:let me know if you(?:'|’)d like|feel free to (?:ask|share|reach out)|I(?:'|’)m happy to (?:help|revise|expand)|hope this helps)[^\n.!?]*[.!?]?\s*$
patterns.rationale: A closing offer is chatbot residue, not part of the requested document.
patterns.action: Delete it unless the communication itself requires an invitation.

patterns.title: Unsupported quality assurance
patterns.rationale: The sentence asserts quality without naming the procedure or evidence that produced it.
patterns.action: Name the validation, coverage, comparison, or test; otherwise delete the assurance.

patterns.title: Throat-clearing opener
patterns.pattern: (?i)(?<!\w)(?:here(?:'|’)s the thing|here(?:'|’)s what I mean|let me be clear|I(?:'|’)ll be honest|to be clear|the uncomfortable truth is|the reality is|the truth is|it turns out|let(?:'|’)s (?:dive in|unpack this|explore this))\s*[:,]?\s*
patterns.rationale: The opener delays a claim that can usually stand on its own.
patterns.action: Delete the opener and state the claim directly.

patterns.title: Faux-insight setup
patterns.pattern: (?i)(?<!\w)(?:what (?:most people|everyone|nobody) (?:miss(?:es)?|get(?:s)? wrong|tell(?:s)? you)|the (?:part|thing|detail) (?:most people|everyone) (?:miss(?:es)?|skip(?:s)?|overlook(?:s)?)|here(?:'|’)s what nobody tells you)\s*[:,]?\s*
patterns.rationale: The setup flatters the writer as the lone holder of an insight instead of supporting the claim.
patterns.action: Remove the setup and let the claim and evidence carry the force.

patterns.title: Interpretive metadiscourse
patterns.pattern: (?i)(?<!\w)(?:it is (?:important|crucial|essential|worthwhile) to (?:note|remember|recognize|recognise|understand) that|the key (?:point|takeaway) is(?: that)?|this (?:point|distinction|finding|detail) matters|as you can see)\s*[:,]?\s*
patterns.rationale: The author tells the reader how to weigh a point instead of showing the consequence or evidence. Ordinary explanatory glosses such as ‘in other words’ are not flagged without a semantic redundancy check.
patterns.action: Delete it when the support is already clear; otherwise add the missing consequence or evidence.

patterns.title: Formulaic binary contrast
patterns.rationale: The not-X-but-Y frame often adds theatrical opposition without adding meaning.
patterns.action: State Y directly unless the correction itself is substantively necessary.

patterns.title: Not-just-but template
patterns.rationale: The construction is often used as a generic emphasis scaffold.
patterns.action: State the stronger claim directly, or retain both clauses only when the distinction is real.

patterns.title: Dramatic colon reveal
patterns.rationale: The label manufactures drama instead of integrating the claim into a sentence.
patterns.action: Rewrite the reveal as a plain declarative sentence.

patterns.title: Superficial participial analysis
patterns.rationale: The trailing clause often labels significance without establishing a mechanism or consequence.
patterns.action: Replace it with the concrete consequence or delete it.

patterns.title: Importance puffery
patterns.pattern: (?i)\b(?:stands? as a testament to|marks? a pivotal moment|plays? a (?:vital|pivotal|crucial) role|solidif(?:y|ies|ied) (?:its|the) position|underscores? (?:its|the) significance|holds? great promise|serves? as a beacon|rich tapestry|cornerstone of)\b
patterns.rationale: The phrase labels importance rather than stating the event, mechanism, or consequence.
patterns.action: State the specific fact and let the reader judge its importance.

patterns.title: Vague attribution
patterns.rationale: The source is too vague for the reader to verify or weigh.
patterns.action: Name and cite the source, or remove the attribution and narrow the claim.

patterns.title: Decorative strong verb
patterns.rationale: The phrase sounds active but usually hides what the subject actually does.
patterns.action: Name the concrete actions, objects, or outcomes.

patterns.title: Weak verb plus nominalisation
patterns.rationale: A weak verb and abstract noun delay the action.
patterns.action: Use the corresponding direct verb where grammar permits.

patterns.title: Wordy filler
patterns.pattern: (?i)(?<!\w)(?:in order to|due to the fact that|for the purpose of|in the event that|at this point in time|with regard to|in relation to|in terms of|on a (?:daily|weekly|monthly|annual) basis|has the ability to|is able to)\b
patterns.rationale: The phrase uses more words than the idea requires.
patterns.action: Replace it with the direct equivalent.

patterns.title: Self-referential signposting
patterns.rationale: The sentence announces nearby content instead of presenting it.
patterns.action: Begin with the claim or retain only a roadmap required by the genre.

patterns.title: Recap ending
patterns.rationale: A generic recap often repeats what the reader has just read.
patterns.action: Delete the label and end on the final concrete implication, decision, or action.

patterns.title: Fake-profound ending
patterns.pattern: (?i)(?:the future (?:isn(?:'|’)t|is not) coming[.;,]\s*it(?:'|’)s already here|this is (?:where|how) the future begins|and that changes everything|the journey (?:has only just|is just) begun|the possibilities are endless|only time will tell)\s*[.!]?\s*$
patterns.rationale: The final line substitutes a generic aphorism for a concrete ending.
patterns.action: Delete it and end on the last specific fact, implication, or next action.

patterns.title: Rhetorical setup
patterns.pattern: (?i)(?<!\w)(?:what if I told you|think about it|imagine this|picture this|plot twist|ask yourself)\s*[:,]?\s*
patterns.rationale: The setup directs the reader's reaction before presenting the substance.
patterns.action: State the substantive point directly.

patterns.title: Self-answered question
patterns.rationale: Question-answer staging can sound templated when a declarative sentence is clearer.
patterns.action: Use the answer as a direct claim unless the question serves a genuine teaching purpose.

patterns.title: Dramatic fragment chain
patterns.rationale: Stacked fragments manufacture punch rather than controlling rhythm around meaning.
patterns.action: Combine the fragments into a complete sentence or keep only the substantive line.

patterns.title: Negative listing
patterns.rationale: The repeated negations delay the positive claim.
patterns.action: State the positive claim directly unless each exclusion changes scope.

patterns.title: Expletive opening
patterns.rationale: The sentence delays its grammatical subject.
patterns.action: Move the real subject and action forward when the rewrite remains natural.

patterns.title: Stacked hedges
patterns.pattern: (?i)\b(?:may potentially|might possibly|could possibly|would perhaps|appears to suggest|seems to indicate|generally tends to|arguably may|perhaps might)\b
patterns.rationale: Multiple hedges obscure the intended level of certainty.
patterns.action: Keep the single hedge that accurately represents the evidence.

patterns.title: Unsupported superlative
patterns.rationale: An evaluative superlative or novelty claim may need a defined comparison set. Ordinary grammatical uses of “most”, “first”, “largest” and “smallest” are not treated as defects.
patterns.action: Name the comparison set and evidence when the phrase makes a substantive claim; otherwise retain the literal wording.

patterns.title: Vague impact claim
patterns.rationale: The phrase asserts impact without naming what changed, for whom, or by how much.
patterns.action: Replace it with the measured outcome, mechanism, beneficiary, and time frame.

patterns.title: Promotional adjective triad
patterns.rationale: A symmetrical adjective triad often supplies promotional rhythm without information.
patterns.action: Keep the one property the text can demonstrate, then provide the evidence.

patterns.title: Sycophantic opener
patterns.rationale: The opener flatters the prompt rather than answering it.
patterns.action: Delete it and begin with the answer.

patterns.title: Reasoning-process leak
patterns.pattern: (?i)\b(?:let me think (?:this through|step by step)|I(?:'|’)ll break (?:this|it) down|breaking (?:this|it) down|here(?:'|’)s my thought process|I need to reason through)\b
patterns.rationale: Internal process narration does not belong in the deliverable.
patterns.action: Delete it and present the result or argument.

patterns.title: Em-dash cluster
patterns.rationale: Multiple em dashes in one paragraph can become a default rhythm rather than a deliberate choice.
patterns.action: Use a period, comma, colon, or parentheses where it clarifies the relation.

patterns.title: Decorative emoji heading
patterns.rationale: The emoji decorates hierarchy instead of expressing document structure.
patterns.action: Use a descriptive heading without the decorative symbol.

patterns.title: Mechanical title-case heading
patterns.rationale: Title case across every heading can create a template-like visual rhythm.
patterns.action: Use the publication's heading convention; otherwise prefer sentence case.

patterns.title: Generic coaching language
patterns.pattern: (?i)\b(?:whether you(?:'|’)re a (?:beginner|seasoned|new|experienced)[^,]{0,60},|you(?:'|’)ll want to make sure|remember, you can always|the key is to)\b
patterns.rationale: Generic coaching addresses an imagined reader rather than the stated audience and task.
patterns.action: Replace it with the direct instruction or audience-specific consequence.

patterns.title: Corporate jargon collocation
patterns.pattern: (?i)\b(?:leverage synergies|move the needle|circle back|low-hanging fruit|deep dive|best-in-class|world-class|game[- ]changer|paradigm shift|end-to-end solution|navigate (?:the )?complexities|unlock (?:the )?potential|harness (?:the )?power)\b
patterns.rationale: The collocation is portable across organisations and usually hides the action or result.
patterns.action: Name the action, constraint, mechanism, or measured result.

patterns.title: Generic world-setting opener
patterns.pattern: (?i)(?<!\w)(?:in today(?:'|’)s (?:fast-paced|rapidly changing|ever-evolving|digital) world|in an era of (?:rapid|unprecedented|constant) change|in the age of (?:AI|technology|digital transformation))[,;:]?\s*
patterns.rationale: The opener supplies generic context that could introduce almost any subject.
patterns.action: Begin with the specific problem, event, or decision.

patterns.title: Portable promotional phrase
patterns.rationale: The phrase can be moved unchanged between products or organisations and says little about the mechanism.
patterns.action: Replace it with the specific action, actor, object, and consequence.
